title: The towers defining integral pullback and completed tensor product are invariant under change of K-flat resolution
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ ($n\geq1$) [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $W$ let $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_W$ be the completed coefficient sheaf on the small pro-etale site $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with projections $\pi_n$, restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_n$ along $\pi_n$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and derived category $D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a tower $(C_n,t_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n)_{n\geq1}$ of complexes of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$-modules write $\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}(C_\bullet)$ for the complex $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$, where $1-s:\prod_nC_n\to\prod_nC_n$, $(c_n)\mapsto(c_n-t_n(c_{n+1}))$, on the termwise products [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. For a complex $P$ of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$-modules put $P_n=P\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}}(A_{E,n})_W$ (termwise change of rings [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]), with the maps $P_{n+1}\to P_n$ induced by $A_{E,n+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_{E,n}$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and $f^*=f^{-1}(-)\otimes_{f^{-1}(A_{E,n})_Y}(A_{E,n})_X$ the module inverse image on sheaves of $(A_{E,n})_Y$-modules [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For complexes $P$ on $Y$ and $P,Q$ on $W$ define

$$
 T_f(P)=\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}_n\operatorname{Res}_nf^*(P_n),\qquad
 T(P,Q)=\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}_n\operatorname{Res}_n\bigl(\operatorname{Tot}(P_n\otimes_{(A_{E,n})_W}Q_n)\bigr),
$$

with direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and transition maps induced by those of $P_\bullet$, $Q_\bullet$. Then: (1) if $u:P\to P'$ and $v:Q\to Q'$ are quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,-}$-modules with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], the induced maps $T_f(P)\to T_f(P')$ and $T(P,Q)\to T(P',Q')$ are quasi-isomorphisms; (2) consequently, choosing for every object a K-flat resolution with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], $K\mapsto T_f(P_K)$ and $(M,N)\mapsto T(P_M,P_N)$ define functors $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ and $D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)^2\to D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$, independent of the resolutions up to a unique isomorphism of functors compatible with their natural comparison isomorphisms on K-flat representatives (these comparisons identify the descended functor with the displayed complex construction after localization), and each value is a derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit] of the corresponding tower in $D(-_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$.

proof.text: For each n apply [lem-pur-change-of-rings-kflat-quasi-iso] to the additive extension-of-scalars functor along the coefficient projection pi_n on the same site: the termwise change-of-rings maps u_n:P_n→P′_n and v_n:Q_n→Q′_n are quasi-isomorphisms. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], all four reduced complexes are K-flat over the finite coefficient sheaf with flat terms. The ring morphism need not be flat; these two results require K-flatness of the input, which is a hypothesis here.

Apply [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] with the finite commutative ring A_{E,n}. Its module inverse image is naturally the tensor-formula f^* used here and is exact, so H^i(f^*u_n)=f^*H^i(u_n) is invertible: f^*u_n is a quasi-isomorphism. No properness or flatness of the scheme morphism is used.

source.place: Exactness statement of prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact; external source Stacks Tag 00WJ

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] on W_proet with ring sheaf (A_{E,n})_W. Its natural identifications Q Tot(P_n⊗Q_n)≅QP_n⊗^L QQ_n identify the image of Tot(u_n⊗v_n) with the derived tensor of the two isomorphisms Qu_n,Qv_n. A bifunctor takes isomorphisms in both variables to isomorphisms (apply it to their inverses). Thus this image is invertible; applying each cohomology functor of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] proves Tot(u_n⊗v_n) is a quasi-isomorphism. This uses the site version of tensor descent, not the ordinary-ring-only lem-pc-kflat-tensor-quasi-iso.

source.place: Tag 06YT (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side), followed by K-flat construction of derived tensor

proof.text: Restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] changes only the action on the same underlying abelian sheaf. Kernels, images and cokernels keep their underlying sheaves and inherit that restricted action; consequently restriction commutes with cohomology and preserves the quasi-isomorphisms just proved. The maps form strict maps of towers: on a tensor generator x⊗a, either reducing first and applying u, or applying u and then reducing, gives u(x)⊗ā. For total tensors the same calculation on x⊗a⊗y⊗b gives u(x)⊗ā⊗v(y)⊗b̄; the direct-sum differential has the same signs on either route. For pullback, write r_n:P_{n+1}→P_n and ρ_n:(A_{E,n+1})_X→(A_{E,n})_X. The transition in the tensor-formula model is f^{-1}(x)⊗a ↦ f^{-1}(r_n)(f^{-1}(x))⊗ρ_n(a). This is balanced: the structure maps c_{n+1},c_n of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] commute with coefficient reduction, since their adjoints send each constant coefficient to the corresponding constant section, and reduction commutes with that prescription before sheafification. Under the canonical identifications of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] this is the underlying abelian-sheaf map f^{-1}(r_n). Naturality of f^{-1} gives f^{-1}(r′_n)f^{-1}(u_{n+1})=f^{-1}(u_n)f^{-1}(r_n); hence the pullback maps too commute strictly with transitions, including the restricted completed coefficient actions. The formulas are verified on presheaf tensor generators and descend by sheafification.

source.place: Termwise coefficient-change construction preceding Tag 06YT; elementary compatibility with quotient ring maps

proof.text: For either strict tower map a_•:C_•→C′_• obtained above let A=∏C_n and A′=∏C′_n. Countable products are exact on the completed module-sheaf category by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]; [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] (2) therefore identifies A,A′ with products in the derived category. The shifted cone of 1−s has its cone triangle by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; rotated, this is exactly the triangle of [def-weil-derived-limit], so each displayed construction is a derived limit. Strict compatibility gives (∏a_n)s=s′(∏a_n); applying ∏a_n to both summands defines the cone map and a morphism of these triangles. Its level components are isomorphisms by steps 2–4. Hence [lem-weil-derived-limit-levelwise-iso] makes the cone map an isomorphism in the derived category. Its cohomology maps are isomorphisms, proving clause (1).

The constructions are functors on complexes: tower maps go to the diagonal product maps on the shifted-cone summands, which preserve identities and compositions. They also respect homotopies. Additive coefficient change and inverse image send dh+hd to dF(h)+F(h)d. Explicitly, if u−u′=dh+hd and v−v′=dk+kd, the total-tensor homotopy from u⊗v to u′⊗v′ on the summand of first degree p is h⊗v+(−1)^p u′⊗k. In dH+Hd the mixed terms cancel by the differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], leaving (u−u′)⊗v+u′⊗(v−v′)=u⊗v−u′⊗v′. With one variable fixed at its identity this also proves the separate-variable assertions. These homotopies commute with the tower transitions. Put h=∏h_n. In the shifted-cone convention d(b,a)=(−db−(1−s)a,da), the degree −1 map H(b,a)=(−hb,ha) satisfies dH+Hd=(∏a_n−∏a′_n) on both summands, since h commutes with 1−s. Thus homotopic input maps give homotopic output maps; the constructions define a functor and a bifunctor on the full K-flat-with-flat-terms homotopy subcategories.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], localization of the full K-flat-with-flat-terms homotopy subcategory at its quasi-isomorphisms is equivalent to the whole derived category. Step 5 shows the functor in step 6 inverts those maps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to descend T_f along this localization, then transport along the equivalence. For T descend first in one variable and then in the other. Naturality extends uniquely at each stage by clause (2) of that universal property; the resulting transformations preserve identities and compositions. This constructs a bifunctor on the product of the two derived categories and natural comparison isomorphisms on K-flat pairs. Inverting quasi-isomorphisms separately suffices: the map (u,v) factors as (u,1) followed by (1,v).

source.place: K-flat localization construction following Tag 06YT; universal property of localization, Stacks Tag 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization)

proof.text: For a chosen resolution q_K:P_K→K from [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], Qq_K is an isomorphism. Compose its image under the descended functor with the comparison on P_K from step 7; this identifies the value at K with T_f(P_K), and likewise in both variables for T(P_M,P_N). Transport the action on morphisms along these identifications: a:K→L acts as i_L F(a)i_K^{-1}, where i_K:F(K)≅T_f(P_K) (and the same formula in each tensor variable). This makes arbitrary objectwise resolution choices into functors without requiring chosen lifts of all morphisms. For a second choice, i′_Ki_K^{-1} gives the natural comparison. [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (2) makes it unique when compatible with the comparison data on K-flat representatives. The last assertion about derived limits was already verified in step 5; no canonical functor on bare towers in a triangulated category is asserted.
